column1: # Real sequencing datasets to process.  ONE dataset per row; edit this file to
# add or remove datasets, then run `bash run_all.sh`.
# This is the only shared file in the pipeline (the simulated pipeline keeps its
# per-tier constants inside each script instead).  A dataset here is a LIST OF
# SRA RUNS or a PRE-BUILT ASSEMBLY, and repeating that across four scripts would
# drift the moment one is added, so the registry is data rather than four copies
# of a constant.  Every script reads it with a dozen lines of stdlib parsing and
# still runs standalone.
# Use `-` for any column that does not apply.  Never leave a cell empty: the
# shell scripts read columns positionally and a trailing empty field is lost.
# Columns
#   dataset         directory-safe name; becomes Data/work/real_<dataset>/ and
#                   the <dataset>__coasm__... run name.
#   study           subdirectory under Data/Real_dataset/ holding the SRA cache
#                   (source=sra) or the assembly (source=assembly).
#   accessions      comma-separated SRA run accessions. Each becomes ONE sample,
#                   i.e. one coverage column - so this list is the differential
#                   coverage signal the binner gets. Fewer than 3 is thin. For
#                   source=assembly this is PROVENANCE ONLY: the runs whose
#                   coverage was adopted, recorded so the dataset can be traced.
#   read_type       short | long.  Decides assembler and minimap2 preset:
#                   short -> metaspades + `-x sr`, long -> metaflye + `-x map-ont`.
#                   Same rule the simulated pipeline applies; a real dataset has
#                   no read simulator, so read_type comes from the run metadata
#                   (SRA "Platform"/"LibraryLayout") rather than from badread/iss.
#                   For source=assembly it records which assembler produced it.
#   viral_enriched  yes | no.  `yes` = the library is already a virome (VLP/TFF
#                   enriched), so every assembled contig is taken as viral and NO
#                   viral-identification tool runs -> run name ends `__noviral`.
#                   `no` = bulk metagenome, so geNomad runs (or its saved calls
#                   are adopted) and only its viral calls are kept -> `__genomad`.
#   source          sra | assembly.
#                     sra      - phase 1 downloads the runs and phase 2 assembles
#                                them. The normal path.
#                     assembly - the assembly already exists; phase 1 imports it
#                                into the work directory and phase 2 skips
#                                straight to the graph. Nothing is re-assembled.
#   assembly_dir    source=assembly only: directory holding the assembly, either
#                   absolute or relative to Data/Real_dataset/. Must contain a
#                   contigs FASTA, a GFA and the assembler's path table
#                   (metaSPAdes: contigs.fasta, assembly_graph_with_scaffolds.gfa
#                   or assembly_graph.gfa, contigs.paths).
#   import_from     optional: a previous run's work directory whose finished
#                   artifacts are adopted into this dataset's work directory
#                   rather than recomputed - `coverage.csv`, the length/viral
#                   filtered `contigs_filt.fasta`, and a geNomad output tree
#                   (`viral/genomad/`). Use `-` to compute everything fresh.
#                   Adopted stages are printed as [adopted] by phase 2, and what
#                   was taken is recorded in the dataset's manifest.json.
#   assembler       optional, source=assembly only. `-` derives it from
#                   read_type (short -> metaspades, long -> metaflye), which is
#                   right when the pipeline assembles. For a PRE-BUILT assembly
#                   the two are independent: the assembly's format is fixed by
#                   whoever produced it, while read_type describes the reads
#                   being mapped for coverage and therefore only picks the
#                   minimap2 preset. Set it when they disagree - e.g. a metaFlye
#                   assembly whose source runs are Illumina.
#   mean_read_length  optional. Normally MEASURED from the FASTQs by phase 2, so
#                   leave it `-`. A pre-built assembly carries no reads to
#                   measure, and the model turns depth back into a read count
#                   with it (reads ~= depth * length / mean_read_length), so an
#                   absent value silently falls back to 126 bp. Set it from the
#                   SRA runs' reported average when the reads are gone.
#   notes           free text, recorded in the dataset manifest.
dataset
aloha_illumina
column11: Station ALOHA (HOT/SCOPE, DeLong Lab) viral TFF metagenomes, Illumina NextSeq 500 paired-end; BioProject PRJNA529454 / SRP189859, the dataset CoCoNet used.

column1: aloha_nanopore
column11: Station ALOHA viral TFF metagenomes, ONT GridION single-end; BioProject PRJNA529454, same study as aloha_illumina.

column1: lake_water
column11: Lake water metagenome, metaSPAdes assembly as distributed with Phables (344,873 contigs). Bulk metagenome, so geNomad calls define the viral set; the saved geNomad run and the 6-sample coverage matrix are adopted from the earlier build rather than recomputed - the reads themselves are no longer on disk. Read length is the SRA-reported average for the 6 runs (595.3 bp per paired spot, 297.7 per read; Illumina HiSeq 2500), not a measurement.

column1: lake_water_megahit
column11: Lake water metagenome, MEGAHIT assembly as distributed with Phables (1,200,868 contigs). SAME six runs and same community as the lake_water row - only the assembler differs, which makes the pair a controlled test of how much the assembly graph matters. Bulk metagenome, so geNomad defines the viral set; nothing is adopted from the metaSPAdes build because every artifact there is keyed to metaSPAdes contigs. Reads were RECOVERED from that build's surviving BAMs (minimap2 -ax sr piped to samtools sort, no -F filter, so unmapped reads were retained) rather than re-downloaded. The distributed GFA names segments NODE_n_length_.., sharing nothing with the k141_n contig names, which would silently produce a zero-edge graph; rename_megahit_gfa.py rewrote them by exact sequence - 1,200,868/1,200,868 matched, all 850,422 links kept. The original is preserved as final.contigs.NODE-names.gfa.

column1: ibd
column11: IBD gut virome, Norman et al. 2015 (WashU), BioProject PRJEB7772. Hecatomb population assembly as distributed with Phables: MEGAHIT per sample merged with Flye --subassemblies, so the layout is metaFlye (assembly_info.txt carries graph_path) while the reads are Illumina MiSeq - read_type=short picks minimap2 -x sr, assembler=metaflye describes the file format. 12 of the study's 171 WGS runs are used, the deepest available (13.1 Gbp): coverage needs SAMPLES not exhaustive depth, and 12 columns is double lake_water's 6, while all 171 would be 101.6 Gbp. The 167 AMPLICON runs are excluded. 95.8% of contigs span >1 graph edge (mean 3.01), so oriented path projection has real material - unlike wastewater, where 22,025/22,035 contigs mapped to one segment and only 10 edges survived.

column1: wastewater
column11: Wastewater virome (U.S. EPA), BioProject PRJNA434744: 18 Illumina MiSeq WGA/MDA runs, 9.4 Gbp, a dilution series (WW_1-100 .. WW_1-100000). Flye-formatted assembly from short reads for the same Hecatomb reason as ibd: MEGAHIT per sample, Flye --subassemblies to merge. read_type=short. Read length is the SRA-reported average (202 bp) for the 18 runs, declared rather than measured, because phase 2 adopted the coverage matrix instead of re-detecting the reads; without it the model defaults to 126 bp and overstates read counts ~1.6x.

column1: soil
column11: Paddy soil virome, Hunan Province China, BioProject PRJNA866269, as distributed with Phables. Hecatomb population assembly (MEGAHIT per sample, merged with Flye --subassemblies), so metaFlye layout with Illumina reads - same arrangement as ibd and wastewater. Only the 12 NovaSeq metagenome runs are used; the other 24 runs in the project are <60 Mbp each and are not metagenomes. Those 12 total 128 Gbp, so reads are fetched PARTIALLY (fastq-dump -X 3000000, ~0.9 Gbp per sample) - coverage needs relative abundance across samples, not depth, and the cohort is only 395 Mbp. CAUTION: the distributed GFA has 2,226 links over 249,193 segments (0.009 links/segment), lower even than wastewater, so the projected contig graph is expected to be near-empty despite 99.3% of contigs carrying a multi-edge graph_path. Kept as a composition/coverage benchmark and as a robustness test for graph-dependent methods.
